That error is not because of your app code. Google is saying the exact key you pasted has expired: `API key expired. Please renew the API key.`

Use Google AI Studio like this:

1. Go to `Google AI Studio`
2. Click `API Keys` in the left sidebar, not `Projects`
3. Open your project or create/select one
4. Create a new Gemini API key
5. Copy the new key and paste it into the app sidebar
6. Generate again

> Task 2: Create a recommendation engine that uses the company data to suggest hotels, activities, ferries, and destinations based on trip inputs.
>
> Goal:
> The app should stop depending only on generic AI output and instead use the company knowledge base to produce stronger, more relevant itinerary context.
>
> Requirements:
> 1. Create a new module:
>    - src/itinerary_app/recommendations.py
> 2. Use the data loader from Task 1.
> 3. Build recommendation functions that use trip type, budget category, number of days, destination, and special requests.
> 4. Return a small, ranked set of recommendations for:
>    - hotels
>    - activities
>    - ferries
>    - destinations
> 5. Keep the logic deterministic and easy to understand.
> 6. Use simple scoring or filtering rules rather than complex machine learning.
> 7. Keep the code easy to debug and extend later.
>
> Expected functions:
> - recommend_hotels(request)
> - recommend_activities(request)
> - recommend_ferries(request)
> - recommend_destinations(request)
>
> Where request is the existing TripRequest model.
>
> Recommendation logic examples:
> - Luxury + Honeymoon should favor premium beachfront resorts.
> - Family should favor family-friendly hotels and relaxed activities.
> - Budget should favor lower nightly prices.
> - Higher number of days can allow more activities and inter-island movement.
> - Special requests should influence activity recommendations.
> - Senior citizen friendly requests should prefer low-activity, low-transfer options.
> - Adventure requests should prioritize activities like scuba diving, snorkeling, and island excursions.
>
> Implementation notes:
> - Return top matches in a clear structured format.
> - Do not invent new hotels or activities if matching rows exist in the CSV files.
> - Prefer exact matches or close matches from the dataset.
> - If no match is found, return a sensible fallback set.
> - Avoid empty results whenever possible.
> - Make the scoring logic easy to understand for staff and future developers.
>
> Output:
> - The recommendation engine should be usable by the UI and prompt builder.
> - Keep the public API clean and stable.

Task 2 is complete and sitting cleanly on top of the Task 1 baseline.

I added the deterministic recommendation engine in [recommendations.py](<./src/itinerary_app/recommendations.py:1>). It reuses the existing Task 1 loaders, scores company data with simple rules, and exposes the four stable functions you asked for: `recommend_hotels`, `recommend_activities`, `recommend_ferries`, and `recommend_destinations` in [recommendations.py](<./src/itinerary_app/recommendations.py:134>).

The logic is intentionally straightforward:
- budget influences hotel and activity pricing scores
- honeymoon, family, adventure, relaxation, and senior-friendly requests adjust rankings
- trip length affects activity count and ferry relevance
- destination and dataset matches are preferred before fallback rows

I also verified it with compile checks and real smoke tests against the Goa sample data. For example, a luxury honeymoon request now ranks `Barefoot at North Goa` first, surfaces scuba and sunset activities, and favors `North Goa` as the top destination. No existing UI, data-loading, or generation flow was changed.
